items.title: Spain and Portugal Clash in World Cup Round of 16
items.body: Spain will face Portugal in the 2026 World Cup Round of 16 on Monday, July 6 at 21:00. The match marks the 42nd encounter between the two Iberian rivals. Portugal won their last meeting in the Nations League final on penalties after a 2-2 draw. The knockout clash is expected to draw massive public attention and could disrupt normal evening routines.

items.title: Feijóo: Spain Cannot Host 8 Million Immigrants
items.body: PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has claimed that Spain is not prepared to host eight million people, accusing the government of pursuing 'non-innocent objectives' through social engineering. His remarks signal a hardening stance on immigration from the main opposition party. The statement highlights a shifting political climate that could shape future policy.

items.title: Regularized Foreigners Fill One-Third of Summer Jobs
items.body: Regularized immigrants will fill roughly one-third of a record 165,584 summer contracts in Spain's tourism sector. The hiring drive aims to ease chronic labor shortages, especially in hospitality. It underscores how regularization has opened doors for foreign workers in a tight job market.

items.title: Flexible Retirement Available for Autónomos from August 28
items.body: From August 28, 2026, self-employed workers (autónomos) can access flexible retirement, receiving 25% of their pension while continuing to work with no income limit. Unlike salaried employees, they are excluded from bonuses and cannot claim a proportional pension. The reform eases the transition into retirement but offers limited financial relief for the self-employed.

items.title: Tax Agency Processes 25.6 Million Returns, Refunds €9.36 Billion
items.body: The tax agency (AEAT) received 25.6 million returns for the 2025 campaign, a 4.6% increase over the previous year. It has already refunded €9.36 billion to 12.95 million taxpayers, while 7.48 million filers owed a combined €24.7 billion—a jump of 20% in payments due. The figures point to stronger employment and improved tax compliance.

items.title: Andalusia PP-Vox Pact Includes €1.3 Billion in Tax Cuts
items.body: The new PP-Vox coalition in Andalusia has agreed to €1.3 billion in tax cuts over four years, including a 0.25% annual reduction in IRPF for incomes under €60,000. New childbirth deductions range from €500 for a first child to over €1,000 for subsequent children. The pact also extends concertados (state-funded private schools) to Bachillerato and reduces subsidies to unions.

items.title: Heatwave Alert: Temperatures to Reach 42°C Starting Sunday
items.body: Spain's AEMET warns of a heatwave from Sunday, July 5 through at least Tuesday, July 7, with maximum temperatures of 42°C in the southwest, river valleys, and inland depressions. The probability is rated medium-high (40-70%). Health authorities urge caution during midday, especially for vulnerable groups and outdoor workers, and advise avoiding prolonged sun exposure.

items.title: Girona Wildfire Forces 45,000 Confinements, Suspect Detained
items.body: A wildfire in the Gavarres Natural Park near Girona has burned 1,300 hectares and forced 45,000 people into confinement across seven municipalities. Around 150 residents were evacuated, including 80 minors from a summer camp. A man has been arrested on suspicion of starting the fire. The Military Emergency Unit has been deployed as the blaze threatens up to 8,000 hectares.

items.title: Airbus Workers in Spain Begin Month-Long Strike
items.body: Airbus employees across Spanish plants started a month-long strike this July over pay and a reduction in telework from two days to one per week starting in September. The SIPA union has rejected salary offers of 3% for 2026 and 2% for 2027, demanding better terms despite record profits. The industrial action could disrupt production and directly affect foreign nationals employed by the aerospace company.

items.title: Ibex 35 Hits Record Close, Nears 20,000 Points
items.body: The Ibex 35 index ended the week at an all-time high of 19,845 points, rising 0.92% on the day. It gained 2.2% for the week and is up 14.7% so far this year. Steelmakers ArcelorMittal and Acerinox surged after the EU imposed a 50% tariff on imported steel. The rally benefits investors, including those holding Spanish equities.

items.title: Government Withdraws Fuel Tax Cuts, Confusing Economists
items.body: The government has quietly removed the fuel tax cuts it approved on March 20 as part of the Iran crisis response. The reversal comes despite oil prices sitting at similar pre-crisis levels, a move economists find puzzling. Pump prices are expected to rise again, hitting the budgets of all motorists in Spain.

items.title: Madrid Pride March to Disrupt City Center Traffic Saturday
items.body: Madrid's Pride state demonstration (MADO 2026) will cause major traffic disruptions on Saturday, July 4 from 19:00, as the parade moves from Glorieta de Carlos V to Plaza de Colón. Over 6,000 security and medical staff will be on duty, and city bus routes will be modified. Road closures are planned throughout the center, requiring alternative routes.
